root_cause: The Node.js test-runner subprocess executing src/bindings/js/node/tests/unit/infer_request.test.js crashed with a native SIGSEGV. The crash is reported at the whole-file level (location :1:1) rather than inside a specific subtest assertion, and the last subtests to report individually completed ('original TypedArray is alive during infer()' passed) are part of the newly-added 'GC safety infer() / inferAsync()' describe block, which repeatedly creates ov.Tensor objects wrapping freshly-allocated Float32Array buffers across async infer()/inferAsync() calls and explicitly exercises V8 garbage-collection timing (including an explicit global.gc() call) to validate that the native addon keeps the underlying TypedArray buffer alive for the duration of native inference. This file and these GC-safety tests are brand new (added in commit 6aabd6aa, merged the same day as this failure) and are exercising native memory-lifetime edge cases in the N-API Tensor/InferRequest bindings (src/bindings/js/node/src/infer_request.cpp, src/bindings/js/node/include/infer_request.hpp) that did not exist before. The failing PR under test (#39321) only touches src/plugins/intel_gpu/src/runtime/ze/ze_ocl_common.hpp (a GPU Level-Zero/OpenCL header-only compile-time check) and runs on CPU infer in this JS test, so the PR diff is unrelated to the crash; the native segfault is most consistent with a pre-existing buffer-lifetime/use-after-free or GC-pinning bug in the new GC-safety test coverage or in the underlying N-API buffer-wrapping code it exercises, not a regression introduced by this specific PR.
reproduction_steps: On a Linux build of OpenVINO with the Node.js bindings enabled: build src/bindings/js/node, then run `node --test tests/unit/infer_request.test.js` from src/bindings/js/node repeatedly (the crash may be intermittent / timing-dependent on GC and async scheduling). Pay particular attention to the 'GC safety infer() / inferAsync()' describe block (lines ~449-505), especially 'original TypedArray is alive during inferAsync()' which calls global.gc() while async infer() promises wrapping freshly-created Tensors/TypedArrays are still in flight.
recommended_actions: Re-run the failed 'OpenVINO JS API (22) / OpenVINO JS API' job; if it passes consistently afterward, this points to flaky/non-deterministic GC-timing-dependent native memory behavior rather than a deterministic crash.

If it crashes again, run the JS Node bindings test suite under a sanitizer (ASan) or with core-dump collection enabled on CI to capture a native stack trace pinpointing the faulting frame (the plain Node TAP output here gives no backtrace).

Review the native buffer-lifetime handling for ov.Tensor/TypedArray wrapping in src/bindings/js/node/src/infer_request.cpp and src/bindings/js/node/include/infer_request.hpp, in particular how references to the backing ArrayBuffer are kept alive (e.g. Napi::Reference/ObjectWrap finalizers) across inferAsync() while the JS GC can run concurrently.
Add CI core-dump / backtrace capture for the Node JS API job so future SIGSEGV failures include a native stack trace instead of only a TAP 'not ok' summary.
prevention_strategies: Enable core-dump collection (e.g., ulimit -c unlimited plus an artifact-upload step for core files, or run under gdb/valgrind in a dedicated diagnostic CI lane) for the Node.js JS API test job so native crashes produce an actionable backtrace rather than just a bare SIGSEGV marker. When adding new tests that deliberately stress GC/async timing (as the new 'GC safety' suite does), consider running them several times in CI or under a stress-test mode before merging, since GC-timing-dependent native bugs are often intermittent.
historical_context: No prior investigation in the CI Doctor MQ database matches this exact signature (infer_request.test.js / GC safety suite / SIGSEGV); this is the first recorded occurrence of a native crash in the OpenVINO JS API Node test runner.
